title: api-config-architecture-sketch-jamie
content:
Quick personal sketch / working notes for API config + routing / KV cache shape.

Context:
- Goal: single, ergonomic config that covers model selection/routing, caching, batching, and fallback policies across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Primary consumers: runtime (C++), router (go service), SDKs (ts/py) which will validate client-side.
- Keep shape small for common cases; allow per-route overrides and an extensible `policies` map for advanced tuning.

Design constraints / heuristics:
- Most routes use a single model + sensible defaults (no user supply required).
- Explicit opt-in for cross-model routing and aggressive caching.
- Separate control-plane config (rollouts/fallbacks) from per-request overrides.
- Config should be JSON-serializable and easy to diff in PRs.

Proposed top-level config shape (flat-ish, minimal fields listed):
- route_name: string (immutable)
- description: string
- default_model: string (model id, e.g. redwood/gpt-4-l)
- model_variants: [string] (ordered by preference; used for fallback/rollouts)
- routing_policy: string enum ["latency-first", "cost-first", "region-preference", "pinned"]
- region: string | null (e.g. us-west1)
- batch_settings: enabled,bool; max_batch_tokens,int; max_batch_size,int; timeout_ms,int -> runtime will pick per-model kernel if batching enabled
- cache: enabled,bool; mode,"prefix"|"full"|"kv-only"; ttl_seconds,int; key_policy,string -> lightweight cache control
- kv_cache: enabled,bool; max_entries,int; eviction,"lru"|"fifo" (for persistent KV reuse across requests)
- fallbacks: list of {model, condition} (condition like "capacity_exhausted" or "latency>500")
- trace_tags: list of strings -> used by observability to tag traces
- eval_prompt_sets: list of eval ids -> linked eval ids for quality monitoring

Note: above uses nested maps for readability here, but stored JSON will be the same. SDK validators will enforce types. For the Drive document we keep the examples.

Examples:
1) Simple hosted route (defaults)
{
  "route_name": "customer-support-chat",
  "default_model": "redwood/assistant-1.0",
  "routing_policy": "latency-first",
  "batch_settings": {"enabled": true, "max_batch_tokens": 1024, "max_batch_size": 8, "timeout_ms": 50},
  "cache": {"enabled": true, "mode": "prefix", "ttl_seconds": 3600, "key_policy": "prompt+user_id"}
}

2) Enterprise route with strict region/pinned model and KV cache
{
  "route_name": "enterprise-finance-summaries",
  "default_model": "redwood/fin-qa-quantized-v2",
  "model_variants": ["redwood/fin-qa-quantized-v2", "redwood/fin-qa-quantized-v1"],
  "routing_policy": "pinned",
  "region": "eu-west2",
  "kv_cache": {"enabled": true, "max_entries": 200000, "eviction": "lru"},
  "cache": {"enabled": false}
}

Routing flow (ASCII diagram):
Client -> API Gateway -> Router Service -> (policy) -> Runtime Pool -> Model Instance
                                          |-> Fallbacks -> Alternate Model
                                          |-> Cache Lookup -> Serve from cache

Notes / open questions/TODOs:
- model_variants semantics: are they strictly fallback order or can router do dynamic weighted routing? (prefer to start fallback-only, then add weights later as separate field: weights: [0.8,0.2])
- caching: need clear semantics for prefix vs full. prefix should allow partial KV reuse while full = exact-match hash. Edge cases for function-calling/tooling responses.
- TTL defaults: propose 1 hour for prefix cache, 24h for KV context entries, configurable per-route.
- SDK validation: disallow `pinned` routing with model_variants missing.
- Compatibility: how to express an autoscaling policy hint? maybe separate orchestration block: autoscale: {min:1, target_qps: X, burst: Y} but keep optional.
- Migration: have a migration tool to convert old route-config YAMLs into this shape; add a "compat_mode" flag.

Performance / implementation notes:
- Runtime should be able to derive kernel selection from (default_model, batch_settings.max_batch_tokens) and expose a best-effort profile in the config UI.
- KV cache should be sharded by route + region to avoid hot shards. Keep monitoring: eviction_rate, hit_rate, avg_lookup_ms.

Action items (for next week):
- Draft a minimal JSON schema for this shape and drop it in the repo (assign: @Samir).
- Add a small runtime PR that accepts the `routing_policy` enum and logs decisions (assign: @Evan).
- Confluence doc: link the detailed decision log and rollout plan (TODO: expand linked_artifacts).

Quick links to references:
- Jira: INF-345 (routing config schema)
- GH PR: serving-runtime/#712 (batching hooks)
- Confluence: API Design Notes (see linked_artifacts)

Random notes/brain dump (scratch):
- Consider `policy: {fallbacks: {on_capacity: modelB}, degrade_to_smaller_inputs: true}` for graceful degradation.
- Might want a cheap "model_score_threshold" to avoid returning obviously broken outputs after a model update.

End of sketch.

---
Small checklist before turning into formal PR:
- [ ] JSON Schema + example fixtures (unit tests)
- [ ] SDK validator update (ts/py)
- [ ] Runtime logging + metrics for routing decisions
- [ ] Migration tool + compatibility tests
- [ ] Product review (privacy/regulatory check for KV caching)

Notes to self: keep this intentionally lightweight; most teams will want small opt-in fields rather than a huge monolith.
